title: Memory-stripe KV allocation with predictive eviction to reduce fragmentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a memory-stripe allocation layer and predictive eviction policy for the KV cache to reduce long-term GPU memory fragmentation while preserving low tail latency for continuous batching workloads.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end alloc/free flow integrates with existing KV API without breaking cache semantics
Mean fragmentation metric (external_hole_ratio) reduced by >= 40% in synthetic mixed-length workloads
No more than 5% regression in P99 request latency under production arrival rates
Automated per-GPU background compaction (coalesce small holes) runs without SLO violations in canary cluster
Canary rollout and automatic rollback hooks implemented in the runtime and Console
technical_plan: Add a thin allocation stripe layer that partitions GPU KV memory into adaptive 'stripes' sized by observed sequence-length histogram
Keep per-stripe free lists and small-chunk free caches to avoid global freelist contention during continuous batching
Implement a predictive eviction policy that uses recent prefix reuse and batch composition signatures to prefer evicting cold entries that cause fragmentation
Introduce a lightweight background coalescer that runs opportunistically when GPU utilization < 60% and respects latency budgets
Expose fragmentation metrics and stripe histograms to Console and use them in Optimize recommendations
Instrument allocation hot paths and add per-op microbenchmarks; integrate with existing tracing hooks
notes: 11/02: Initial design proposal drafted; trade-off discussion around stripe size — fixed vs adaptive. Chose adaptive (histogram-driven) to avoid overpartitioning.
11/04: Spike showed adaptive stripes reduce small-hole creation by ~30% on sequence mixes with 8-512 token ranges.
11/06: Decided to keep allocation metadata under 64 bytes per stripe to minimize overhead on smaller GPUs.
11/08: PM review: include Console surfacing and an Optimize recommendation to toggle background coalescer for Dedicated customers.
11/09: Design review with runtime team: concurrency model approved; micro-locks on per-stripe free lists preferred over global locks.
Trade-offs: predictive eviction adds heuristics which may cause temporary misses for extremely bursty customers; mitigated via canary and safe-fallback to LRU
risks: Predictive heuristics misclassify hot items during phase shifts in workload, causing increased tail latency
Background coalescing might compete with kernel scheduling on memory-bound models if thresholds are miscalibrated
Additional allocation metadata increases resident memory slightly, impacting very constrained GPUs
Complexity of stripe resizing could introduce fragmentation spikes if done synchronously
metrics: P50/P95/P99 inference latency as observed in continuous-batching mode
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert if mean_fragmentation_per_gpu > 0.25 for more than 30 minutes in production
Alert if background coalescer runtime > 1s per invocation on GPUs with active inference
Dashboard showing stripe-size distribution, per-stripe free-list depth, and eviction decisions over time
Synthetic scenario job that runs weekly to validate fragmentation regression for mixed-length traces
rollout_plan: 2) Internal canary on non-critical Dedicated pool with conservative coalescer thresholds
3) Expand canary to 5% of production traffic for 48 hours; monitor latency/fragmentation metrics
4) Release to Dedicated customers with opt-in via Console toggle for first month
5) Gradual enable for Hosted tier after no regressions for 2 weeks
6) Enable automatic Optimize recommendation once stable
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator invariants (no leaks, no double-free)
Integration test with continuous-batching harness replicating production arrival patterns
Chaos test: simulate sudden sequence-length distribution shift and verify graceful behavior
Perf benchmark against baseline (current allocator) using 24-hour mixed trace replay
